rooms.name: 🌀 Teleporter Room 🌀
rooms.short_description: A circular chamber of dark metal with a repaired, blue-glowing teleporter platform, scattered cargo crates, and panoramic windows overlooking space and Orthos.
rooms.details:
The teleporter room is a large, circular chamber of dark metal, its curved walls illuminated by soft, recessed lighting. The room is mostly empty, apart from a few cargo crates scattered along the walls and a broad, circular platform embedded in the center of the floor.

Dominating the far wall are enormous panoramic windows, revealing a breathtaking view of space. Countless stars glitter against the darkness, while the immense blue-and-white curve of Orthos fills much of the view to the right. Swirling clouds drift over vast oceans and continents, with the planet's atmosphere glowing faintly along its horizon.

At the center of the chamber, the circular platform emits a soft blue glow. Its surface is covered in intricate geometric patterns, surrounded by a ring of luminous symbols in an unfamiliar script. Several sections of the platform appear to have been recently repaired, with newer metal panels, fresh welds, and replacement components contrasting with the older, scuffed machinery. A few exposed conduits pulse faintly with light.

A heavy, airtight door is set into one wall, its reinforced frame showing signs of frequent use. Small signs bearing strange symbols are mounted nearby, some engraved into metal and others formed from thin strands of glowing wire.

The room is otherwise quiet, save for the low hum of the central platform and the faint vibration of the station's machinery.

Several signs are mounted on and around the window.

On the wall beside the window
An octagonal sheet of scorched hull-plating is welded directly onto the wall, featuring raw binary code and circuit paths deeply gouged into the metal with a plasma cutter.
STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY: MANDATORY. VACUUM: LETHAL. IMPACT: 0% TOLERANCE.
On the center of the glass pane
A neon-orange triangular sticker is slapped haphazardly onto the center of the glass pane, featuring a crude hand-drawn pictogram of a stick figure exploding next to a "thumbs-up" icon.
DO NOT YEET THE SEPARATING-THINGS. SPACE IS COLD AF. VIBE CHECK = FAILED.
To the left of the window
A humming acrylic box is mounted crookedly to the left of the window, housing flickering blue neon tubes that occasionally show the phantom image of a cracked pane before resetting.
CAUTION: GLASS (CURRENTLY) INTACT. AVOID BLUNT FORCE AT 12:42 PM YESTERDAY.
Hanging from the ceiling over the window
A shimmering silk banner with gold-tasseled fringes hangs from the ceiling over the window, featuring elegant, sweeping golden calligraphy that glows softly in the starlight.
Gaze upon the infinite void, but do not invite it within, for the breath of the faithful is a gift to be guarded. By the will of the Hierophant.
Across the bottom corner of the window frame
A metal slinky is stretched across the bottom corner of the window frame, with individual colorful letters dangling from the metal coils that bounce whenever anyone walks past.
If the glass breaks, we all get a free trip to the moon! Downside: It's a one-way trip and you'll be a human popsicle. Don't tap the fishbowl!

rooms.name: Main Corridor-Part 1
rooms.short_description: A long, wide corridor of scuffed dark metal beneath soft white strip lighting. Airtight doors, alien signs, reinforced windows, and security bulkheads line the station's main artery.
rooms.details:
A long, wide corridor of dark metal extends so far into the distance that its far end is difficult to make out. Continuous strips of soft white light run along the upper edges of the walls, illuminating a floor of broad, smooth metal panels. The panels bear countless faint scuffs and scratches from years of foot traffic and cargo transport, but the corridor is clean and well-maintained.

Heavy, airtight doors line both sides of the passageway at irregular intervals. Some are narrow personnel hatches, while others are wide enough to accommodate vehicles or large equipment. Around nearly every doorway is a collection of small signs bearing strange runes, abstract symbols, and unfamiliar alien scripts. Their styles vary wildly: engraved metal plaques, glowing wire, carved stone, and even what appears to be handwriting permanently sealed beneath transparent coatings. Some are neatly mounted, while others hang crookedly or occupy peculiar positions around the doorframes.

Between some of the doors, broad reinforced windows offer glimpses into the rooms beyond. Through one, an impossibly lush forest glows with bioluminescent plants beneath an artificial sky. Another reveals a workshop crowded with arcane instruments, shelves of colorful reagents, and a brightly burning forge. Other stretches of the corridor have no windows at all, leaving the purposes of the rooms behind their sealed doors a mystery.

At regular intervals, thick seams cross the ceiling, walls, and floor, marking where massive security bulkheads can descend to seal off entire sections of the passage. Small recessed indicator lights glow beside these barriers, and reinforced tracks are built directly into the surrounding metal.

A faint, steady hum of ventilation and distant machinery fills the air. Despite the variety of strange environments concealed behind its doors, the corridor itself feels almost mundane—a practical, heavily traveled artery connecting the station's countless disparate chambers.

rooms.name: Workshop
rooms.short_description: An enormous, orderly workshop combining a roaring stone forge, advanced machinery, and arcane workbenches. Mostly empty supply shelves line the walls, and smaller craft areas extend beyond the main chamber.
rooms.details:
The enormous workshop's dark metal walls are illuminated by the warm orange glow of a roaring forge and the cooler blue light of several unfamiliar machines. The air smells of hot iron, machine oil, and alchemical reagents, while the steady crackle of flames mingles with the quiet hum of electrical equipment.

Workbenches of wildly different styles fill the chamber. Heavy wooden tables hold anvils, hammers, tongs, and other traditional blacksmithing tools, while nearby metal workstations are equipped with glowing diagnostic screens, articulated mechanical arms, and intricate devices of uncertain purpose. Other benches are covered with alchemical glassware, crystalline apparatuses, rune-engraving instruments, and partially assembled magical contraptions. A few contain strange combinations of all three, as though generations of craftsmen from entirely different civilizations have shared the same workspace.

Along the walls, tall shelves and cabinets hold an assortment of raw materials, spare parts, and crafting supplies. Most are conspicuously empty, with only scattered metal ingots, coils of wire, bottles of reagents, and unfamiliar components remaining. Small permanent signs in various alien scripts mark the storage areas, some engraved into metal, others painted or formed from faintly glowing runes.

A large stone forge is built into the far wall, its flames burning steadily beneath a heavy arch of soot-darkened masonry. Nearby, an assortment of anvils, quenching troughs, and mechanical fabrication equipment suggests that both traditional smithing and advanced manufacturing take place here.

Along one wall, a broad reinforced window looks out into the station's main corridor, beside a heavy airtight door. Beyond the central workshop, the immense room continues into a series of smaller work areas, partially concealed behind partitions, shelves, and banks of machinery. Each appears dedicated to a different craft, with its own distinctive tools and equipment.

Despite the mismatched furnishings and centuries of accumulated technology, the workshop is surprisingly orderly. Tools are arranged within easy reach, work surfaces are mostly clear, and the floor shows only the expected scuffs and burn marks of a heavily used industrial space. The combination of medieval craftsmanship, arcane experimentation, and futuristic engineering gives the room the impression of a place where almost anything could be built, repaired, or reinvented.

rooms.name: Forest
rooms.short_description: A vast forest beneath a tiled artificial daytime sky, with a winding path and a stream. An artificial tree projects a caretaker dryad, and a cleansed druidic altar stands to the north.
rooms.details:
A vast forest extends into the distance beneath an artificial daytime sky assembled from tiled screens high above the canopy. A metal bulkhead is visible through the trees on the right, but the rest of the landscape appears natural.

A path winds through the trees and dense vegetation, while a stream flows through the forest, providing drinkable water. Strange plants and animals inhabit the woodland, some of which may be edible.

Artificial Tree

A clearing contains a tree of impossible symmetry, every leaf perfect and undamaged. Close inspection reveals its artificial construction and a glowing handprint. Touching the handprint causes an illusory dryad to appear. The construct provides information about the forest’s health and manages its environmental systems, including artificial rainfall and the flow of the stream. It also appears to have information about the ship.

Druidic Altar

A massive druidic altar stands in the northern portion of the forest. Tiered stone platforms, broad steps, and curved standing stones surround a central ritual space, with spiral carvings marking the stonework. The corruption that once tainted the site has been cleared, leaving it less ominous and more in keeping with the surrounding woodland.

The altar sustains a ritual that promotes the forest’s growth. A nature spirit was once imprisoned here, but it has since been freed.

Residents

A flock of house drakes, relocated from The Lighthouse, now lives in the forest.

rooms.name: Orrery Archive
rooms.short_description: A dim archive of towering bookshelves surrounding an enormous brass-and-steel orrery of unfamiliar planets. A glowing artificial sun lights a spiraling observation walkway, while animated brooms sweep the floor.
rooms.details:
The Orrery Archive is a vast, dimly lit chamber where the station's dark metal architecture gives way to towering bookshelves, aged brass, and intricate clockwork machinery. The air carries the faint scent of old parchment, machine oil, and ozone, while a gentle mechanical hum reverberates through the room.

Dominating the center of the chamber is an enormous orrery, its intricate framework of brass and blackened steel extending outward from a brilliant, golden sphere suspended above the floor. The artificial sun radiates a warm, steady light, casting long shadows across the surrounding machinery. From its base, slender mechanical arms extend in sweeping arcs, supporting a collection of slowly orbiting planets.

The planets themselves are strange and unfamiliar. One is a translucent globe filled with drifting, luminous motes. Another appears shattered, its fragments held together by flickering strands of energy. A third bears rings of shimmering liquid metal that continually unravel and reform. The entire apparatus moves with an almost unnatural precision, its gears turning silently beneath the soft hum of hidden machinery.

A broad, curved walkway rises from the floor and spirals around the central mechanism, allowing closer inspection of the orbiting spheres. Small observation platforms branch from its sides, holding an assortment of brass instruments, crystalline lenses, and unfamiliar control devices. The walkway's surface is worn smooth from years of use, and one section appears to have been recently repaired with newer, mismatched metal.

Beyond the orrery, the chamber's outer walls are lined from floor to ceiling with immense bookshelves, their countless volumes forming a dense, irregular patchwork of colors and materials. Leather-bound tomes sit beside metal tablets, rolled scrolls, and books covered in unfamiliar organic-looking substances. Narrow ladders run along the shelves, while scattered reading desks and mismatched chairs occupy the spaces between them, illuminated by small floating orbs of pale light.

Small signs in alien scripts are scattered throughout the archive. Crooked metal plaques hang near the entrance, translucent tags dangle from the walkway railings, and strange symbols shimmer faintly above certain shelves. One particularly modern-looking sign, formed from glowing geometric lines, stands out near the repaired section of the walkway.

The chamber is otherwise quiet, filled with little more than the faint rustling of old pages, the steady, rhythmic movement of the great orrery, and the sweeping of animated brooms cleaning the floor. Occasionally, one of the orbiting planets seems to hesitate or jump slightly along its path before resuming its measured course. The shifting light casts peculiar shadows across the bookshelves, giving the entire archive an unsettling sense of movement, even in moments of apparent stillness.

rooms.name: Small Hallway above Orrery Archive
rooms.short_description: A short hallway with a heavy metal door at one end and a spiral staircase down at the other end. A smaller metal door is on each of side of the hallway.

rooms.name: Restoration Engine
rooms.short_description: A massive repair engine lies beneath twenty feet of cooling water, surrounded by grated catwalks leading to a glowing central pad. Four shielded vortices rise through ceiling openings, bathing the metal chamber in pulsing pale-blue light.
rooms.details:
The Restoration Engine occupies a metal chamber filled with cool air that carries the scent of water, ozone, and a faint metallic tang. Its heavy, airtight door opens with a hiss.

A massive arcane machine capable of repairing almost any damage to an item lies submerged in twenty feet of water to keep it cool. At the center of the room, a large pad emits a steady blue glow. Narrow grated bridges connect it to catwalks that cling to the perimeter walls, their surfaces slick with condensation.

Beneath the pad, a central shaft descends through the water to a complex device with eight protrusions, each covered in glyphs and unfamiliar symbols. Warm wall lamps glint off the surrounding metalwork, contrasting with the light-blue radiance pulsing through the magical machinery and reflecting across the water.

Strange control panels line the south, west, and east walls. Their shifting glyphs and alien symbols pulse in time with the machine below.

In the northeast, southeast, northwest, and southwest corners, contained vortices of magical energy spiral upward from circles scribed into metal rings on the floor. A transparent cylindrical field constrains each portal’s power, channeling its blue energy through an opening in the ceiling. The columns hum softly.

The entire chamber has an atmosphere of tightly controlled power, every pulse of light and ripple of water suggesting immense energy held just barely in balance.

South Control Panel

A wide console of dark metal and inset glass is covered in softly glowing glyphs arranged in concentric patterns. The symbols shift slowly, rearranging themselves when not directly observed. Thin filaments of light connect different sections of the panel, forming temporary paths that fade and reform.

West Control Panel

This station is more mechanical, with levered arms, rotating dials, and sliding plates etched with deep, angular runes. The components resist movement slightly, as though unused for a long time, yet respond with precise, deliberate clicks when adjusted. A faint vibration travels through the metal whenever a control is manipulated.

East Control Panel

The most alien of the three stations is a vertical surface embedded with crystalline protrusions and smooth depressions sized for hands, or something like hands. Symbols float just beneath the surface, drifting like suspended ink. Touching the panel causes the glyphs to scatter and reform elsewhere.

rooms.name: Hanging Registry
rooms.short_description: A dim, hushed chamber filled with suspended metal nameplates, preserving memories of those left behind. Blank plates gleam among the inscriptions, and the clusters shift silently despite the still air.
rooms.details:
The Hanging Registry is a dim, metallic chamber filled with dense clusters of thin plates suspended from the ceiling on fine wires. Hanging at varied heights, they form a shifting forest of etched metal. Each plate bears names in countless scripts—some carefully engraved, others jagged or uneven, as though carved in haste or desperation. Small lights near the floor cast isolated pools of illumination and catch pale reflections on the suspended plates.

The air is unnaturally still, and every sound is dampened, swallowed almost immediately. Footsteps land without echo, voices fall flat, and even the faint hum of the station seems absent here.

Among the countless inscribed plates, some hang blank. These empty surfaces draw the eye, their smooth metal subtly reflective yet wrong, as if waiting. Standing near them creates a faint, creeping sensation, like a word just out of reach or a memory that refuses to form.

The plates occasionally shift, ever so slightly, despite the lack of airflow—soft, silent movements that suggest unseen patterns or quiet rearrangement.

rooms.name: Porcelain Passageways
rooms.short_description: A vast, pristine chamber of glowing white tiles, marble bathtubs, and brass faucets pouring strange substances. Balconies and oddly angled stairs rise above pearlescent mist.
rooms.details:
The Porcelain Passageways form a chamber so bright and immaculate that it barely seems real.

The room is vast, far larger than the corridors leading to it would suggest. Every visible surface is covered in small, glossy white hexagonal tiles, each set with thin, dark grout that creates an endless geometric pattern across floor, walls, pillars, stairs, and ceiling alike. The effect is almost hypnotic. The usual dark metal bones of the station are nearly invisible here, buried beneath an obsessive layer of porcelain-bright order. The room rises through multiple levels, opening upward into a towering interior lined with balconies, alcoves, and mezzanines, all reached by staircases of the same white-tiled construction. Some stairs rise in straightforward lines; others seem to hang at unsettling angles or terminate at levels that do not quite make intuitive architectural sense, as though the room obeys its own private geometry.

Rows of freestanding bathtubs fill the lower floor, each carved from smooth white marble and standing on clawed feet. Between and beyond them are polished ceramic sinks mounted to the tiled walls, fitted with heavy brass faucets and valves whose industrial heft clashes with the chamber's nearly celestial whiteness. Similar tubs occupy the upper levels, arranged with unnerving precision, each perfectly spaced and waiting in complete stillness. Despite their variety of placements and elevations, the whole room seems arranged according to some careful, ritual logic.

From many of the brass fixtures, strange substances pour continuously. Some basins receive a thick, shimmering silver fluid, translucent and luminous, with tiny internal swirls that resemble drifting nebulae or liquid starlight caught in suspension. Other faucets pour a rich, viscous golden liquid, heavy as perfumed oil, glowing warmly as it pools in the tubs below. The surfaces of these fluids ripple lazily, casting faint, shifting reflections of silver, gold, and iridescent color onto the surrounding white tile. High overhead, these caustic glimmers tremble across the ceiling like ghostly auroras.

The room's illumination seems to come from nowhere and everywhere at once. The tiles themselves radiate a soft, sourceless white glow, bright enough to banish harsh shadows entirely. The result is clinical, almost flattening, as though depth itself is being gently washed away. The strange fluids add their own secondary life to the space, so that pale rainbows and metallic sheens drift faintly over the otherwise sterile geometry.

A thin mist clings to the floor, pearlescent and cool, swirling softly around the feet of the tubs and the bases of the sinks. It obscures their lower edges just enough to lend the room a dreamlike weightlessness, as though the fixtures might be floating. The air smells faintly floral and mineral at once: sharp cleanliness, warm oil, damp stone, and some sweeter perfume that does not quite mask the sterile undertone.

Along the walls and tucked into corners are the station's ever-present signs, especially stark against the white surfaces. Small circular plaques of dark carved metal interrupt the tiles at odd intervals, mounted at waist height or fitted into unexpected recesses. Their jagged runes glow in dim colors: violet, pink, and blue-white. They provide the only sharp contrast in the room besides the brass and the magical liquids. None are in English. Some appear carefully aligned; others are ever so slightly crooked, as though placed by different hands across different eras.

Though the room resembles a bathhouse, a washroom, or perhaps some sort of cleansing facility, its silence gives it a stranger character. No voices echo here. No splashing sounds break the stillness beyond the steady pouring of impossible liquids into marble basins. The whole chamber is unnervingly pristine, serene to the point of discomfort, with the atmosphere of a place of purification, treatment, or ritual preparation.

Beautiful and spotless, the chamber carries an unsettling uncertainty about what, exactly, it was meant to cleanse.

rooms.name: Quartermaster's Bazaar
rooms.short_description: A T-shaped bazaar packed with vending machines. The main entrance is at the base, Kleb Rosh-Nak’s automated shop occupies the intersection, and the east and west ends lead to other areas.
rooms.details:
The Quartermaster’s Bazaar is a T-shaped corridor of dark ribbed metal, crowded and almost claustrophobic. The main entrance lies at the base of the T, opening onto a long, narrow passage that meets an east-west corridor at Kleb Rosh-Nak’s shop. Exits at the east and west ends lead to other areas. Recessed alcoves line both sides from floor to ceiling, packed so tightly with vending modules, display cases, and layered shelving that the walls seem to press inward. The station’s metal structure is still visible beneath everything, but it has been overwhelmed by generations of additions, retrofits, and improvised merchant logic.

Inside the cases is a bewildering jumble of goods. Sleek chrome components and microchips are stacked beside leather-bound grimoires, bundles of wire, forged daggers, alchemical flasks, glowing fuel canisters, cracked crystal lenses, preserved specimens, coils of tubing, packets of dried herbs, and stranger objects whose purpose is not immediately clear. Nothing seems sorted in a way that makes sense to outsiders, yet everything looks as though it belongs exactly where it is. Layers of alien price tags, inventory marks, and coded stickers overlap one another on nearly every transparent surface.

The lighting is aggressive and chaotic. Harsh pulses of electric blue, neon pink, acid green, and pale gold flash from flickering vending screens and display panels, while warmer pools of light come from old-fashioned lanterns mounted between the cases. Those lanterns look almost antique, but they hum faintly with hidden power. Overhead, exposed conduits and pneumatic tubes crowd the ceiling in a tangled network. Every few moments, small sealed containers shoot through them with sharp rattles and hissing bursts, vanishing deeper into the Bazaar’s unseen logistics.

Almost every section of wall offers some kind of interaction point. Holographic control panels shimmer with static and half-legible symbols. Brass or iron pull-levers jut out beside touchscreens. Rusted coin slots are carved into distorted, stylized faces. Small drawers sit beneath larger cases, some latched shut, others twitching open and closed as internal mechanisms continue their work. The whole place resembles a market that has been built, rebuilt, patched, overloaded, and then left to keep running forever.

The floor is broad enough for comfortable passage, but only barely. Its metal panels are scuffed, grimy, and worn smooth by immense traffic over many years. Grease-darkened streaks, boot marks, and dragged scratches cross the walkway, while the air smells of hot circuitry, old oil, ozone, dust, and the faint sharpness of alchemical reagents. Despite the clutter, the Bazaar is very much alive: mechanisms click, screens buzz, tubes hiss, and something somewhere is always dispensing, sorting, or restocking.

The station’s strange signage is everywhere. Small permanent signs in mismatched styles cluster around individual modules and major interfaces: glowing wire sigils, stamped metal plates, painted warnings sealed under lacquer, and dangling tags in scripts that range from rune-like to wholly alien. None are in English. Some are neatly placed; others are mounted crookedly or tucked into improbable corners, as though added piecemeal over the Bazaar’s long life.

The entire corridor resembles an ecosystem of trade: cramped, overbuilt, grimy, and bizarrely functional. Whatever the station’s inhabitants once needed—whether magical, mechanical, sacred, or mundane—it seems they came here to get it.

Kleb’s Shop

At the intersection of the entrance passage and the east-west corridor stands a powerful automated shop built from interlocking arcs of dark metal and translucent enchanted glass. It is larger and more sophisticated than the rest of the Bazaar, like a shrine or throne of commerce at the heart of the Bazaar. Its structure seems subtly unfinished, or perhaps perpetually reconfiguring itself. Exposed gears turn with slow precision behind clear panels, while glowing script crawls across its surfaces like living inventory ledgers. Drawers slide open and shut without being touched. Compartments unfold into trays, small work surfaces, or delivery chutes before collapsing back into the structure.

Dominating the machine’s façade is a great emblem of burnished alloy: the symbol of Kleb Rosh-Nak, suspended within a rotating halo of tool-shaped sigils. It pulses faintly, as if acknowledging every transaction and every piece of inventory that passes through the system. The whole machine radiates a workshop-like warmth despite its mechanical exactness, and every surface hums with potent divine energy. There is no obvious keyboard, handle, or payment slot for a newcomer to use. Instead, in the center of the main console, a single familiar handprint glows softly, waiting.

rooms.name: Main Corridor-Part 2
rooms.short_description: A long, wide corridor of scuffed dark metal beneath soft white strip lighting. Airtight doors, alien signs, reinforced windows, and security bulkheads line the station's main artery.
rooms.details:
A long, wide corridor of dark metal extends so far into the distance that its far end is difficult to make out. Continuous strips of soft white light run along the upper edges of the walls, illuminating a floor of broad, smooth metal panels. The panels bear countless faint scuffs and scratches from years of foot traffic and cargo transport, but the corridor is clean and well-maintained.

Heavy, airtight doors line both sides of the passageway at irregular intervals. Some are narrow personnel hatches, while others are wide enough to accommodate vehicles or large equipment. Around nearly every doorway is a collection of small signs bearing strange runes, abstract symbols, and unfamiliar alien scripts. Their styles vary wildly: engraved metal plaques, glowing wire, carved stone, and even what appears to be handwriting permanently sealed beneath transparent coatings. Some are neatly mounted, while others hang crookedly or occupy peculiar positions around the doorframes.

Between some of the doors, broad reinforced windows offer glimpses into the rooms beyond. Through one, an impossibly lush forest glows with bioluminescent plants beneath an artificial sky. Another reveals a workshop crowded with arcane instruments, shelves of colorful reagents, and a brightly burning forge. Other stretches of the corridor have no windows at all, leaving the purposes of the rooms behind their sealed doors a mystery.

At regular intervals, thick seams cross the ceiling, walls, and floor, marking where massive security bulkheads can descend to seal off entire sections of the passage. Small recessed indicator lights glow beside these barriers, and reinforced tracks are built directly into the surrounding metal.

A faint, steady hum of ventilation and distant machinery fills the air. Despite the variety of strange environments concealed behind its doors, the corridor itself feels almost mundane—a practical, heavily traveled artery connecting the station's countless disparate chambers.

rooms.name: Aetherlift Hangar
rooms.short_description: A high-ceilinged hangar containing crystal-powered hovering passenger and cargo carriages, energized parking berths, maintenance workstations, and an enormous reinforced bulkhead door.
rooms.details:
The Aetherlift Hangar is a broad, high-ceilinged chamber of dark metal. Its ribbed ceiling is lined with recessed panels of soft white light. The room resembles a large vehicle garage, with orderly rows of small, open-sided carriages, each roughly the size of a golf cart. Some have multiple rows of bench seating for passengers, while others have a single driver's seat and a flat cargo bed.

Rather than wheels, each vehicle rests a few inches above the floor, suspended by glowing crystals and slowly rotating metal rings beneath its chassis. Faintly luminous sigils spiral across the floor of each parking berth, feeding energy into the vehicles with a gentle, musical hum. Occasionally, a carriage drifts slightly before correcting itself with a soft chime.

Along one wall, maintenance benches are stocked with specialized tools, crystal components, mechanical parts, and a mixture of arcane instruments and advanced diagnostic equipment. Small, strangely shaped signs bearing unfamiliar runes and alien symbols hang above the workstations and vehicle bays.

Dominating the far wall is an enormous reinforced bulkhead door, wide enough for several vehicles to pass through side by side. Its heavy segmented panels are set into the station's metal structure, and the floor leading toward it bears the polished scuffs of frequent traffic.

The room is clean and well-maintained, though its machinery and fittings show years of use. The air carries a faint scent of ozone and warm metal, accompanied by the constant, quiet resonance of the hovering vehicles.

rooms.name: The Celestial Threshold
rooms.short_description: A star-filled chamber with a dark, glasslike floor, two enormous luminous dragon figures, and a swirling portal.
rooms.details:
The station seems to vanish around visitors as they step through the doorway.

Beyond the doorway stretches an immense, star-filled void. The floor appears to be perfectly smooth black glass, or perhaps something entirely transparent, revealing countless stars glittering in the darkness below. Thin lines of pale light connect some of these stars into strange, unfamiliar constellations.

Flanking the chamber are two enormous dragons, their serpentine bodies curving along the left and right sides of the room. They appear to be statues made entirely of pale blue-white light, their scales, claws, and elaborate horns traced in luminous strands like constellations given form. Their massive heads turn towards the entrance, as if inspecting visitors.

At the far end of the chamber, a swirling portal hangs suspended in the darkness, its shifting radiance casting faint ripples of light across the floor.

The air is cool and unnaturally still. Sound seems strangely muted, and a faint, almost imperceptible hum fills the space. Nothing moves except the occasional drifting mote of starlight and the slow, hypnotic swirling of the distant portal.

rooms.name: The Celestial Reliquary
rooms.short_description: A circular platform suspended in a star-filled void, surrounded by eight luminous statues, with the Astravindicta hovering at its center.
rooms.details:
Visitors emerge from the portal at the top of a short flight of stairs, looking out across a vast circular platform suspended in an endless, star-filled void. There are no visible walls, ceiling, or planets—only the distant shimmer of countless stars. Thin lines of pale blue light connect some of them into unfamiliar constellations, stretching across the darkness in every direction.

The platform itself appears to be made of dark, polished material, almost indistinguishable from the surrounding void. Its surface glitters with tiny points of light, giving the unsettling impression that visitors are standing directly upon the stars.

Arranged evenly around the platform are eight enormous statues, each resting on a circular pedestal. Their forms depict strange, unfamiliar beings, rendered in stylized, almost abstract shapes. Some resemble humanoids, while others have distinctly alien features, including elongated limbs, elaborate crests, and unusual facial structures. Rather than solid stone, the statues appear to be formed from translucent blue crystal or condensed starlight, their features traced in faintly glowing lines. Small points of brighter light shine from their eyes.

At the exact center of the chamber, a brilliant ring of pale blue runes surrounds a mysterious object suspended just above the floor. The artifact is roughly the size of a basketball, a perfect sphere of pale crystal held within an intricate golden framework. Its polished bands are covered in impossibly fine runic inscriptions, surrounding a central golden seal.

Within the crystal, an entire galaxy appears to swirl in miniature. Countless stars spiral slowly around a luminous center, casting shifting patterns of blue, white, and gold across the surrounding floor.

The chamber is utterly silent, save for a deep, almost imperceptible vibration that seems to come from the artifact itself. Despite the impossible expanse surrounding the platform, the air is still and breathable, and the distant stars provide a soft, ethereal illumination.

Astravindicta - The Vengeance of the Stars

Suspended silently in the air is an exquisite spherical artifact, roughly the size of a basketball. Its surface is made of flawless, transparent crystal, enclosed within an intricate lattice of interwoven golden filaments. The delicate framework forms elaborate geometric patterns, with intersecting curves and diamond-shaped ornaments that seem as much a work of art as a feat of impossible engineering.

At the sphere's apex sits a circular golden seal, engraved with a ring of impossibly fine runes surrounding a raised, diamond-shaped emblem. The inscriptions emit a faint blue-white glow, their shapes unfamiliar and their meaning inscrutable.

Within the crystal sphere, an entire spiral galaxy appears to exist in miniature. Countless stars swirl around a brilliant golden-white center, their luminous arms stretching outward in shimmering shades of violet, blue, and silver. The galaxy turns almost imperceptibly, with tiny points of light occasionally flaring and fading among its countless stars. Upon close inspection, the depth within the sphere seems impossible, as though its crystal surface were a window into an actual expanse of space rather than a container for an illusion.

The artifact slowly spins, radiating a gentle blue and golden light. A faint, rhythmic vibration can be felt in the air around it, more like a distant heartbeat than the hum of machinery. Despite its delicate appearance, the sphere conveys an unsettling sense of permanence and immense, carefully contained power.

Despite its incredible power, the object seems to invite observers to reach out and touch it.

rooms.name: Hall of Fallen Worlds
rooms.short_description: A circular chamber resembling an ancient temple, with murals and shrines depicting flourishing worlds descending into divine war and destruction.
rooms.details:
The Hall of Fallen Worlds is a vast, circular chamber, its walls lined with towering stone pillars and intricate carvings. Unlike the rest of the station, the room resembles an ancient temple, its weathered stone illuminated by soft, golden light.

At the center stands a massive, freestanding wall bearing an elaborate mural divided into five horizontal scenes. The uppermost depicts a prosperous civilization, with bustling cities, fertile fields, and peaceful settlements. Below it, the scenes grow progressively darker: gods and celestial beings gathering above opposing armies, a terrible war between divine forces, and the devastation left in its wake. The final panel shows the world consumed by an enormous, fiery cataclysm, leaving nothing but ruin.

Around the chamber's outer wall, dozens of shallow alcoves contain smaller shrines, each displaying its own variation of the central mural. The inhabitants differ wildly between them: insect-like humanoids, amorphous beings of living slime, crystalline creatures, and countless other unfamiliar species. Their cities, landscapes, and gods are equally diverse, yet every mural follows the same progression—from flourishing civilization to divine war, and finally, utter destruction.

The chamber is unnaturally quiet. The air carries a faint scent of ancient stone and incense, and the countless shrines stand in solemn silence, each seemingly commemorating an entire world lost to the same terrible fate.

Prominent Alcoves

1: The Void-Threaders (The Spiders)

Mural: An immense forest of silver trees supports cities of intricate webs, inhabited by elegant, many-legged beings. Above the forest, two opposing pantheons of spider-like deities battle across an enormous celestial web. Gods with luminous golden limbs tear at the threads while dark, many-eyed divinities drag entire constellations into the void. Below them, the world's supporting webs unravel, sending cities and their inhabitants falling into darkness.

Shrine: A tiny, perfectly preserved silver web is stretched between four black crystal pillars, with a single translucent egg suspended at its center.

A delicate, irregular web of glowing blue fiber-optic threads is stretched across a small bronze frame suspended from the top of the mural's stone arch, its intricate knots casting overlapping shadows that form flowing three-dimensional script.
With the deepest humility, we present the account of our beloved ancestral home, whose countless beautiful threads were severed by the regrettable disagreement of those exalted beings entrusted with its preservation. May our lost world be remembered with the dignity it was denied.

2: Binary-7 "Maintenance" Cult

Mural: A sprawling mechanical civilization covers an entire planet in enormous towers, gears, and industrial complexes. Above it, two armies of metallic gods wage war. One faction consists of immense, angular beings carrying weapons of lightning, while the other resembles intricate clockwork titans surrounded by orbiting rings of fire. Their conflict shatters the planet's machinery while millions of tiny mechanical inhabitants attempt hopeless repairs.

Shrine: A small mechanical heart rests on a steel pedestal, its gears moving slowly despite being disconnected from any power source.

A heavy octagonal plate of recycled steel is welded directly beneath the mural, bearing vertical columns of brutally deep binary scratches and jagged circuit diagrams carved with an industrial plasma cutter.
ORIGIN WORLD. OPERATIONAL. GODS FOUGHT. SYSTEM FAILURE. TOTAL LOSS. RECORD RETAINED.

3: The Jelly-Kin of Ooze-9

Mural: A magnificent underwater civilization of translucent towers and floating crystalline structures is inhabited by colorful, spherical slime creatures. Some wear tall pointed hats balanced on their gelatinous bodies, while others carry toolbelts, tiny backpacks, or decorative headbands. Above the ocean, two rival groups of immense aquatic deities clash: beautiful beings of flowing water and coral struggle against monstrous figures of boiling steam, salt, and burning sunlight. Their battle splits the seas apart, exposing the inhabitants to a devastating sky.

Shrine: A small transparent bowl holds a perfectly spherical drop of brilliant blue slime that floats just above its surface, surrounded by several tiny, abandoned hats.

A rounded, translucent glass dish filled with softly glowing emerald slime is suction-cupped to the polished stone border beneath the mural, its slowly shifting bioluminescent swirls forming fluid characters that pulse with gentle light.
This was our beautiful home, where every tide carried a thousand friends. The gods broke the seas, and our world dried away. We remember the waters, and everyone who swam beside us.

4: The Fragmented (Exile Spirits)

Mural: A beautiful city of impossibly slender towers stands beneath a violet sky, populated by pale, ethereal humanoids whose features seem almost recognizable. Above the city, several luminous gods struggle against a host of shadowy divine figures, pulling the landscape apart like pieces of torn parchment. The inhabitants themselves are torn into ghostly fragments, drifting through the ruins as disembodied shadows.

A long, narrow scroll of tattered parchment hangs crookedly from the left side of the mural, covered in mismatched characters cut from ancient books and documents that remain slightly blurred unless viewed through a reflective surface.
Here is the place where we were whole. Here are the streets where we walked, the faces we loved, and the names we once possessed. The gods took our world, but they shall not take its memory.

5: The H-0RS3 "Riders"

Mural: An enormous city of colorful, soaring highways and floating platforms stretches across a brilliant landscape beneath three suns. Thousands of strange riders race across the sky on mechanical and living mounts. Above them, two rival groups of celestial beings charge against one another on magnificent divine steeds, their collisions shattering the highways and sending the entire civilization falling into darkness.

Shrine: A pair of battered riding goggles and a small, brightly painted wheel rest on a low stone shelf, accompanied by a faded photograph of several riders standing together.

A small triangular plate of faded neon-orange plastic is permanently affixed to the stone beneath the mural, its Ever-Ink pictograms depicting a radiant planet, laughing faces, clasped hands, several colliding divine figures, and a final black circle.
This was our world. We rode without fear. We believed tomorrow would always come. Then the gods went to war, and tomorrow never came.

6: The Lithos-Architects

Mural: A monumental civilization of living stone giants inhabits cities carved directly into vast mountain ranges. Above them, opposing pantheons of colossal stone deities wield mountains as weapons. One faction appears carved from gleaming marble, while the other resembles living obsidian. Their blows crack the continents and reduce the seemingly eternal civilization to rubble.

Shrine: A miniature stone city, carved with astonishing precision, sits on a massive block of granite, its tiny towers painstakingly repaired with seams of gold.

A thick rectangular slab of black basalt is embedded into the stone pedestal beneath the mural, its deeply chiseled geometric cuneiform radiating faint warmth from a handful of particularly important symbols.
OUR WORLD STOOD FOR NINE MILLION YEARS. WE BUILT FOR ETERNITY. THE GODS REQUIRED SEVEN DAYS TO DESTROY IT. LET THIS STONE ENDURE LONGER THAN THEY DID.

7: The Glimmer-Flys

Mural: A dazzling world of enormous crystalline flowers and floating islands is populated by tiny winged beings with iridescent bodies. Their cities glitter beneath a rainbow-colored sky. High above, two swarms of luminous deities clash, some resembling enormous jeweled insects and others radiant humanoids with wings of pure light. Their brilliance burns the delicate civilization to ash.

A narrow strip of iridescent ribbon is pinned vertically to the carved stone beside the mural with tiny crystalline needles, its hundreds of rapidly spinning mirrored sequins forming fleeting symbols in reflected light.
OUR WORLD. OUR LIGHT. THE GODS FOUGHT. ALL DARK.

8: The Bureau-Kraken

Mural: A vast, perfectly ordered mechanical civilization stretches across an enormous geometric world of interlocking gears, precisely aligned towers, and concentric cities. Its inhabitants are exclusively Modrons, ranging from simple, spherical Monodrones and rectangular Duodrones to increasingly complex, many-sided beings, all performing their assigned duties in a harmonious society governed by absolute mathematical order. Above them, two opposing armies of deities wage war, their chaotic conflict violating the fundamental laws of the Modrons' existence. One divine faction wields radiant geometric weapons, while the other commands turbulent storms of impossible shapes and colors. As their battle intensifies, the world's perfectly symmetrical structures twist into irrational configurations, gears break apart, and countless Modrons are crushed or scattered into the void. The mural is itself arranged in rigid geometric sections, with every figure and event depicted in exacting mathematical proportions.

Shrine: A miniature filing cabinet constructed from polished brass sits upon a perfectly level stone pedestal, containing thousands of impossibly small documents organized according to an elaborate classification system. Beside it stands a tiny, inactive Monodrone, its single eye permanently closed and its wings folded neatly against its spherical body.

A perfectly rectangular sheet of laminated white paper is permanently adhered to the stone pedestal beneath the mural, covered in microscopic Gothic lettering arranged into hundreds of precisely aligned paragraphs, numbered subdivisions, and detailed legal footnotes.
OFFICIAL RECORD OF CIVILIZATIONAL TERMINATION: This mural serves as the final authorized account of the sovereign Modron civilization formerly occupying the designated origin world. Said world's destruction occurred as a direct consequence of armed hostilities between entities classified as Divine Powers, resulting in the irreversible disruption of established mathematical order and the loss of all governmental, computational, mechanical, and administrative infrastructure. An estimated 99.997% of assigned personnel failed to complete their designated duties. No formal declaration of hostilities was received. No appeal was permitted. No compensation was provided. This incident remains under review.
A small brass plaque beneath the tiny, inactive Monodrone bears impeccably engraved Modron script.
EMPLOYEE #000000001. DUTY STATUS: INCOMPLETE. REASSIGNMENT: PENDING.

9: The Rust-Walkers

Mural: A once-magnificent metallic world stretches beneath a copper-colored sky, its inhabitants resembling humanoid beings fashioned from polished iron and bronze. Above them, rival pantheons of flame-wreathed and storm-shrouded deities battle across the heavens. Their conflict transforms the gleaming planet into a corroded wasteland as its cities crumble into red dust.

Shrine: A shallow iron bowl contains a small pile of reddish dust, beneath which the remains of a delicate metal flower are barely visible.

A circular disk of heavily corroded iron is bolted to the stone floor immediately beneath the mural, its concentric rings of reddish corrosion forming chemical characters that smell faintly of ozone and wet metal.
This was our world before the rust. We believed our works would outlast the heavens. Then the gods fought, and even the heavens began to decay. All things return to dust. Our world was merely the first.

10: The Star-Singers

Mural: A magnificent city of crystalline towers stands amid rolling hills beneath a sky filled with musical constellations. Graceful inhabitants gather in enormous amphitheaters while two celestial choirs of gods wage war using visible waves of sound. The divine choirs appear arranged in opposing semicircles, their harmonies colliding violently and shattering the towers, mountains, and finally the planet itself.

Shrine: A small crystal music box sits beneath the mural, playing a single, haunting note that seems to continue long after it should have faded.

A delicate crescent of curved glass tubes filled with softly vibrating silver sand is mounted beneath the mural's gilded frame, its musical staffs and notes forming elegant script that produces a mournful harmony when touched.
Here is the world that first taught us to sing. Here is the song of its people, silenced when the gods raised their voices against one another. Though our world is gone, its final note shall never fade.

11: The Hive-Mind of Sector 4

Mural: An enormous insectoid civilization inhabits a world covered in vast honeycomb cities and towering organic spires. Millions of small figures are connected by delicate golden threads representing their shared consciousness. Above them, two opposing swarms of insect-like gods tear apart the celestial web linking the inhabitants, shattering both the cities and the collective mind.

Shrine: A small honeycomb structure rests within a glass case, its individual cells containing tiny amber spheres that glow faintly when approached.

A rough oval patch of dark burlap is pressed permanently into the stone border beside the mural, its overlapping amber and violet pheromone stains forming intricate organic patterns that emit a sweet, mournful fragrance.
This is the memory of the world we shared. All minds were one, all lives belonged to all others. The divine war severed the great connection, and our world fell silent. Those who remain carry the voices of those who cannot.

12: The Chronos-Glitchers

Mural: A strange civilization is depicted in several overlapping versions of itself: a primitive village, a magnificent futuristic metropolis, and a ruined wasteland all occupy the same landscape. Above them, two immense deities battle across different moments in time. One appears youthful and radiant while the other is ancient and skeletal, their struggle causing entire centuries to collapse into one another until the planet simply disappears.

A small, crooked rectangular box of translucent acrylic is mounted beside the mural, containing flickering violet and cyan neon tubes whose glowing characters occasionally display different versions of the same inscription.
This was our world. This will have been our world. We remember its destruction yesterday, tomorrow, and before it was born. The gods fought, and every moment we might have lived was taken from us.

13: The Trash-Goblins (Scavenger Guild)

Mural: A sprawling civilization of small, goblin-like creatures has built a thriving city from the wreckage of ancient machines, enormous discarded vessels, and mountains of salvaged metal. Above them, numerous colossal gods battle amid falling stars. Some wield enormous celestial tools, while others command storms of fire and lightning, crushing the beloved city beneath mountains of burning debris.

Shrine: A small pile of carefully arranged junk—rusted gears, bent nails, broken toys, and colorful scraps of metal—has been lovingly assembled into the shape of a tiny city.

A flattened rectangular sheet of salvaged tin is crudely riveted to the stone ledge beneath the mural, covered in thick charcoal stick figures depicting a planet, countless small inhabitants, several enormous fighting figures, and a field of black X marks.
THIS WAS HOME. WE FOUND THE BROKEN THINGS AND MADE THEM BEAUTIFUL. WE BUILT A WHOLE WORLD FROM WHAT OTHERS LEFT BEHIND. THEN THE GODS BROKE EVERYTHING AGAIN. NOTHING LEFT TO FIX.

14: The Order of the Void-Eye

Mural: A civilization of tall, faceless beings inhabits a world of black towers and enormous circular openings that look out into absolute darkness. Above the world, several radiant gods wage war against a host of dark, indistinct divine entities. Their battle floods the world with blinding light, consuming the shadow-dwelling inhabitants until only empty silhouettes remain.

A small square sheet of perfectly matte-black silicone is mounted over a concealed light within the mural's stone frame, its precisely cut negative-space characters projecting delicate inscriptions onto the stone below.
This is the history of our world, which once flourished unseen. We believed that what remained hidden would remain safe. But when the gods made war, even the darkness could offer no sanctuary.

15: The Party-Bot Renegades

Mural: A joyous mechanical civilization fills a planet-sized city with brilliant lights, colorful towers, and enormous gathering places where thousands of robots celebrate beneath artificial stars. Above them, two opposing groups of immense mechanical gods clash, sending waves of destructive energy through the city and extinguishing its lights one district at a time.

Shrine: A small, motionless disco ball hangs above a pair of worn dancing shoes, surrounded by faded streamers and several unlit glowsticks.

A small, cracked rectangular display screen is permanently attached to the stone pedestal beneath the mural with faded neon duct tape, its damaged pixels forming a flickering rainbow inscription whose final line has been burned away.

Note: Damaged. A dark burn mark has destroyed the bottom portion of the screen, permanently obscuring the final sentence.

We built a world where no one had to be alone. There was music in every street and light in every home. Then the gods came, and the lights went out. [Final line unreadable.]

16: The Hierophant's Hand

Mural: A breathtaking civilization of golden temples, celestial gardens, and soaring white towers stretches across a fertile world. Its inhabitants kneel in prayer as two magnificent pantheons of winged gods wage war in the heavens. Some gods are adorned in gold and silver, while others wear dark armor and wield blazing weapons. Their divine conflict rains destruction upon the cities and sanctuaries below.

Shrine: A small golden altar holds a pair of extinguished candles, a cracked ceremonial chalice, and a tiny silver figurine of a kneeling worshiper.

A narrow banner of ivory silk embroidered with elaborate golden calligraphy hangs from a silver bracket beside the mural, its gold-tasseled fringe resting against the stone and its sweeping characters adorned with tiny halos.
Behold the sacred remembrance of our world, where countless faithful souls raised their voices in devotion. When the heavens turned against themselves, our prayers could not stay the destruction. Let all who witness this testament remember that even the most blessed world may perish beneath divine wrath. By the will of the Hierophant.

17: The Station Normals

Mural: Unlike the other murals, this one is visibly the work of dozens of different artists, each contributing a piece of a larger composition. Some sections depict peaceful villages in simple, almost childish styles, while others show detailed cities, forests, mountains, and oceans painted with remarkable skill. The inhabitants are equally varied, with humans, insectoids, reptilians, mechanical beings, and countless other species appearing alongside one another. Above them, the divine war is portrayed as an enormous, chaotic struggle between many different gods, each painted in a different artistic style. Despite the mismatched techniques, the mural forms a coherent whole, emphasizing the shared destruction of countless ordinary lives.

Shrine: A simple wooden shelf holds a collection of small personal objects: a child's drawing, a worn cooking spoon, a broken pair of spectacles, a faded photograph, and several handwritten notes in different languages.

A small square sheet of plain white paper is carefully taped to the bottom edge of the mural's ornate stone frame, bearing neat black block letters without any decoration or ornamentation.
This is a picture of our homes before they were destroyed. We were ordinary people living ordinary lives. We had families, friends, and places we loved. When the gods went to war, none of that mattered. Please remember us.

18: The Vacuum-Born

Mural: A dark, airless world is surrounded by enormous orbital structures and transparent habitation domes, inhabited by tall, slender beings moving through the vacuum between them. Above the planet, two vast armies of deities engage in a catastrophic celestial war. One faction consists of radiant, winged beings wielding weapons of light, while the other appears as monstrous, many-limbed entities surrounded by swirling darkness. Their battle tears apart the orbital structures and splits the planet into an expanding field of debris. Unlike the other murals, the divine figures have been deliberately defaced, their faces chiseled away and their bodies scarred with deep gouges.

Shrine: A small black pedestal holds a smooth, perfectly spherical fragment of their shattered world, surrounded by a thin ring of transparent material bearing microscopic inscriptions.

A perfectly transparent hexagonal sheet of thick plexiglass is embedded flush against the stone beside the mural, its microscopic geometric etchings becoming visible only when illuminated at a precise 45-degree angle.
Origin world: Lost. Orbital habitats: Destroyed. Planetary integrity: Zero. Cause: Divine conflict. Population before event: 18,402,771,006. Population after event: 0. Responsible entities: Gods. Classification: Enemies of All Living Worlds. Forgiveness: Impossible. Retribution: Pending.

19: The Re-Animators

Mural: An unsettling but beautiful living world is depicted, its cities formed from enormous organic structures resembling bones, muscles, and translucent membranes. Its inhabitants are strange stitched-together beings living harmoniously among the organic architecture. Above them, two pantheons of skeletal and flesh-bound deities wage war, tearing the world's living tissues apart and causing its inhabitants to collapse. At the very bottom of the mural, however, a small group of survivors carries a pulsating organic seed away from the dying planet, suggesting that their story has not yet ended.

Shrine: A small glass vessel contains a pulsating mass of red organic tissue suspended in a clear nutrient solution, with tiny veins extending from it toward the vessel's walls.

A small oval sheet of cured leather is stretched across a frame of polished bone attached to the stone pedestal beneath the mural, its veined characters formed from dark surgical sutures and cauterized burn marks.
This was the body that carried us all. Its mountains were our bones, its rivers our blood, and its forests our lungs. When the gods made war, they tore open the flesh of our world and left it to die. But death is not the end of life. We remember every tissue, every organ, every heartbeat. One day, we shall find a new body for our world, and it shall live again.

20: The Gravity-Drunks

Mural: An impossible world of floating oceans, inverted mountains, and cities suspended in every conceivable orientation is inhabited by cheerful humanoids traveling between drifting islands. Above the planet, two opposing factions of gravity-wielding gods battle, twisting space into violent spirals. The floating continents are ripped apart and scattered across the void, while the inhabitants struggle helplessly against forces they once controlled.

Shrine: A tiny floating stone platform is suspended within a glass sphere, upon which rests a miniature house that remains perfectly upright no matter how the sphere is turned.

A small spherical sign of smooth blue rubber is permanently suspended from a thin chain attached to the mural's stone arch, its spiraling lenticular letters appearing to fall endlessly across the surface as the viewer moves around it.
This is the world where we learned to fly without wings, where the oceans hung above our heads and the mountains floated beside us. When the gods fought, they stole the forces that held our home together. We have wandered ever since, searching for a place to land.

rooms.name: Portable Portal Nexus
rooms.short_description: A circular magitech chamber containing a ringed central apparatus and four pedestal machines, each holding a compact runic metal disk.
rooms.details:
Portable Portal Nexus is a large, circular chamber of dark metal, illuminated by soft white lights recessed into the walls and ceiling. The room is remarkably clean, with a broad, open floor surrounding an imposing magitech apparatus at its center.

The central device is a towering construction of dark steel, polished brass, and faintly glowing crystal. Several concentric metal rings encircle a raised circular platform, their surfaces densely engraved with intricate runes, geometric patterns, and unfamiliar symbols. Thick cables and crystalline conduits run from the base into the floor, while small points of blue-violet light pulse slowly across its surface. A low, resonant hum fills the chamber, occasionally accompanied by a faint crackle of arcane energy.

Equally spaced around the central apparatus stand four identical machines, each resembling a sturdy metal pedestal fitted with articulated clamps and delicate mechanical instruments. Suspended within each machine is a strange, compact object: a thick, circular disk of dark metal, roughly the size of a dinner plate, its surface covered in tightly interlocking geometric segments and tiny, luminous runes. Each disk rests motionless within its housing, connected by several fine, glowing contacts.

The floor between the central apparatus and the four surrounding machines is marked by thin lines of inlaid metal, forming a precise, symmetrical pattern. Along the walls, small signs of varying shapes and materials display indecipherable symbols in several unfamiliar scripts. Some glow faintly, while others are simply engraved into metal plates.

Despite the complexity of the machinery, the room is strangely still. Nothing appears to be moving beyond the slow pulse of the lights, and the steady hum of the central device seems almost to reverberate through the floor beneath visitors' feet.

rooms.name: Main Corridor-Part 3
rooms.short_description: A long, wide corridor of scuffed dark metal beneath soft white strip lighting. Airtight doors, alien signs, reinforced windows, and security bulkheads line the station's main artery.
rooms.details:
A long, wide corridor of dark metal extends so far into the distance that its far end is difficult to make out. Continuous strips of soft white light run along the upper edges of the walls, illuminating a floor of broad, smooth metal panels. The panels bear countless faint scuffs and scratches from years of foot traffic and cargo transport, but the corridor is clean and well-maintained.

Heavy, airtight doors line both sides of the passageway at irregular intervals. Some are narrow personnel hatches, while others are wide enough to accommodate vehicles or large equipment. Around nearly every doorway is a collection of small signs bearing strange runes, abstract symbols, and unfamiliar alien scripts. Their styles vary wildly: engraved metal plaques, glowing wire, carved stone, and even what appears to be handwriting permanently sealed beneath transparent coatings. Some are neatly mounted, while others hang crookedly or occupy peculiar positions around the doorframes.

Between some of the doors, broad reinforced windows offer glimpses into the rooms beyond. Through one, an impossibly lush forest glows with bioluminescent plants beneath an artificial sky. Another reveals a workshop crowded with arcane instruments, shelves of colorful reagents, and a brightly burning forge. Other stretches of the corridor have no windows at all, leaving the purposes of the rooms behind their sealed doors a mystery.

At regular intervals, thick seams cross the ceiling, walls, and floor, marking where massive security bulkheads can descend to seal off entire sections of the passage. Small recessed indicator lights glow beside these barriers, and reinforced tracks are built directly into the surrounding metal.

A faint, steady hum of ventilation and distant machinery fills the air. Despite the variety of strange environments concealed behind its doors, the corridor itself feels almost mundane—a practical, heavily traveled artery connecting the station's countless disparate chambers.

characters.name: Ariana Isenhart
characters.physical_description: Muscular, soot-streaked arms, hair pulled into a practical bun; always carrying a toolkit and a whetstone.
characters.personality: Precise, disciplined, quietly confident; speaks little but commands respect with her skill.
characters.other_details: Travels with Aurethion. Acts an armorer--assists in keeping his gear maintained, as well as making minor adjustments.

characters.name: Arvek (Arvie) Spotsnout-Smith
characters.physical_description: This small Ratfolk has light brown fur and a white patch around his pink nose. He wears clothing with many pockets stuffed with small tools.

characters.name: Aurethion
characters.physical_description: Tall and imposing, partially draconic with gleaming scales integrated into custom-forged plate armor.
characters.personality: Honorable to a fault and protective almost to excess; struggles between draconic pride and knightly humility.

characters.name: Britt Underfoot
characters.physical_description: Small and nimble, with quick fingers and bright green eyes; wears light leather armor and a utility belt full of tools.
characters.personality: Curious, cheerful, and slightly mischievous; always the first to explore a new ruin or tunnel.

characters.name: Elias Windhook
characters.physical_description: An elderly man, dressed in fisherman's garb; carries a fishing pole and tacklebox
characters.personality: Cheerful, friendly, relaxed

characters.name: Fennick Glimmerfoot
characters.physical_description: Tiny, radiant, greenish hair with floral accents; carries a small flute.
characters.personality: Cheerful, whimsical, loves playing pranks and keeping the group laughing.
characters.other_details: Travels with Britt Underfoot. Companion and morale booster; helps make long expeditions fun and engaging.

characters.name: Ganizadi Glyphroot
characters.physical_description: Luminous pale blue core encased in a dark oak wooden exoskeleton, deeply carved with symbols and glyphs representing language and knowledge. Fragments of paper and ink float subtly around the core.
characters.personality: Slightly eccentric and intensely focused on patterns in language and history. Speaks in layered metaphors, enjoys unraveling ancient texts, and delights in sharing philosophical insights.

characters.name: Gideon
characters.physical_description: A small, elderly-looking poppet wizard with piercing blue eyes, bushy gray eyebrows, and a long silver-gray beard. Wears a blue robe and oversized pointed hat adorned with stars and crescent moons. Carries a flame-tipped wooden staff and keeps magical trinkets on his belt.
characters.personality: Eccentric artificer. Obsessed with magical constructs and devices.

characters.name: Hilda Stoutbrew
characters.physical_description: Young, round-cheeked, auburn hair in a short braid; simple tunic with Helkara’s holy symbol pinned on. Always carrying a small flask of ale and a satchel of healing herbs.
characters.personality: Eager, respectful, and a little clumsy; devoted to learning brewing, healing, and hospitality from Thalra. Loves seeing others smile and is quick to help with chores or small tasks.
characters.other_details: Travels with Thalra Brewmantle. Acolyte and apprentice cleric; learns rituals, healing techniques, and the holy ways of Helkara directly from Thalra.

characters.name: Lunexa Duskweaver
characters.physical_description: Shadow-touched humanoid with faint gray skin; carries floating notepads and quills.
characters.personality: Quiet, thoughtful, and creative; excels at observing patterns in Runeweaver’s work.
characters.other_details: Travels with Runeweaver. Record-keeper; documents experiments and provides subtle insight to improve workflow.

characters.name: Lyria Moonthread
characters.physical_description: Slender, dark hair tied back, robes slightly too long; carries notebooks, quills, and a small crystal orb.
characters.personality: Inquisitive, attentive, patient; fascinated by Veylorin's spells and constantly takes notes.
characters.other_details: Travels with Veylorin Starweaver. Apprentice; learns arcane theory and assists with spell research.

characters.name: Mira Brightleaf
characters.physical_description: Youthful, luminous purple core encased in a wooden exoskeleton; carries a small lyre and floating sheets of notes.
characters.personality: Cheerful, encouraging, and talkative; keeps the group engaged during long research sessions.
characters.other_details: Travels with Ganizadi. Companion and morale booster; prevents Ganizadi from becoming too socially isolated while helping with note-taking.

characters.name: Runeweaver
characters.physical_description: Tall metallic frame with reinforced plating and tool mounts along the limbs. Integrated stabilizers help maintain balance under heavy loads. Optical sensors glow softly in dim light.
characters.personality: Stoic, methodical, and extremely precise. Constantly tests innovations under stress to improve performance and is deeply protective of allies in battle.
characters.other_details: Innovation: Reinforced Exosuit, a personal armor enhancement that deploys stabilizing braces and adaptive shields to improve defense and mobility.

characters.name: Rurik Pebbleleaf
characters.physical_description: Plant-like, dwarf-height humanoid; leafy hair and a small satchel of scrolls and ink bottles.
characters.personality: Methodical and loyal; loves organizing Ganizadi's research, taking meticulous notes, and cross-referencing texts.
characters.other_details: Travels with Ganizadi. Junior apprentice; shadows Ganizadi during research, learning analysis and pattern recognition.

characters.name: Sentinel Varr
characters.physical_description: Human-sized; made of bronze-colored metal with glowing blue components; the symbol of ship security is built into his chassis
characters.personality: Serious; protective of the ship; strongly dislikes chaos in all forms
characters.other_details: Rescued from the brig in Security. Was confined there for "several centuries".

characters.name: Sir Greg*
characters.physical_description: Gleaming, excessively gold-trimmed armor; a flowing crimson cape that billows without wind; perfectly styled hair he fixes mid-fight; and a cosmetically glowing longsword. Maintains a striking heroic pose at all times.
characters.personality: Speaks in grand declarations, interrupts others to monologue, interprets disagreement as villainy, and escalates immediately to violence. Cannot admit defeat, insisting every loss was merely a test.
characters.other_details: *Champion of Light, Scourge of Darkness, Hero of Destiny, Unquestioned Victor, Bearer of Eternal Triumph. Remember it well, villain!

characters.name: Tahlok Shardframe
characters.physical_description: Sleek metallic body, small glowing nodes, tool compartments along limbs; optical sensors blink softly.
characters.personality: Methodical and precise; logs experimental data carefully and assists Runeweaver with calculations.
characters.other_details: Travels with Runeweaver. Apprentice and assistant; helps with schematics, diagrams, and small technical tests.

characters.name: Thalra Brewmantle
characters.physical_description: Stocky and strong, with auburn hair braided with golden beads. Wears chainmail and a pendant engraved with Helkara's holy symbols. Carries a reinforced battle tankard that doubles as a weapon and a small satchel of healing supplies.
characters.personality: Warm, nurturing, jovial, and steadfast; protective of her allies and always ready with a healing word or frothy mug of ale to lift spirits.

characters.name: Tilly
characters.physical_description: Small, doll-like poppet with a body woven from tightly braided straw and twine, rosy cheeks, expressive dark eyes, and lavender-silver hair styled into two long, thick braids. Wears a crimson robe adorned with turquoise geometric embroidery and tassels, a teal scarf fastened with golden bells, and two knitting-needle-like antennae protruding from the top of her head.
characters.personality: Shy but friendly, speaks with a stammer; loves cooking

characters.name: Tink Gearwhistle
characters.physical_description: Small, copper hair sticking out of a messy cap; always carrying tiny tools and vials.
characters.personality: Eager, excitable, curious; constantly experimenting under Britt's guidance.
characters.other_details: Travels with Britt Underfoot. Apprentice and assistant; helps Britt prepare tools, maps, and traps.

characters.name: Torren Alderforge
characters.physical_description: Broad-shouldered and powerfully built. He is bald, with a full, meticulously maintained beard touched by dignified streaks of gray. Magical tattoos formed from luminous crystal trace across his skin, glowing softly and occasionally shifting patterns.
characters.personality: Friendly, outgoing, and effortlessly welcoming, with a talent for making strangers feel like regulars. He genuinely cares for his patrons and readily offers advice, comfort, or a discreet favor. Beneath his warmth lies a practical business owner who understands that generosity has limits and even a timeless tavern must turn a profit.
characters.other_details: Proprietor and bartender of The Crystal Mug, an enigmatic tavern that appears in different places and eras. He remembers countless patrons, cultures, and events, though he carefully avoids revealing knowledge that could disrupt history. No matter where The Crystal Mug appears, Torren is always behind the bar, polishing a glass and ready to greet whoever walks through its door.

characters.name: Veylorin Starweaver
characters.physical_description: Tall and slender, with silver-white hair cascading over a deep blue robe adorned with arcane sigils. Carries a glowing magical staff, and three shimmering Aeon stones orbit his head, faintly illuminating his face.
characters.personality: Brilliant, focused, and precise; loves experimentation and mastering destructive magic, though somewhat absent-minded socially. Analytical and strategic in combat, often serving as the party's magical powerhouse.

character_groups.short_description: A small group of NPCs researching the mysteries of the ship.
character_groups.name: Researchers

npc_groups.name: The Void-Threaders (The Spiders)
npc_groups.lettering: A complex web of glowing fiber-optic wires stretched across frames. The "letters" are formed by the intersections and knots in the wire.
npc_groups.language_oddities: The language is three-dimensional. To a human, it looks like a mess of tangles, but from the correct angle, the shadows cast by the wires form legible sentences.
npc_groups.signage_physical_form: Irregular, hand-spun wire lattices shaped like jagged webs. They are usually hooked into ceiling corners rather than eye-level walls.
npc_groups.communication_quirks: They are extremely polite and formal, viewing direct eye contact or blunt speech as a sign of primitive aggression. Their signs often use flowery, overly-long descriptions for simple rooms (e.g., "The Chamber of Nutritious Repose" for a cafeteria).
npc_groups.common_appearance: Spider‑folk with eight‑limbed features, chitinous accents, and silk‑looming motifs; often wear subtle cords and climbing gear that accentuate their limbs.
npc_groups.demeanor: Highly formal and polite with one another; to outsiders, overly deferential and elaborate in speech, often using circumlocutions.

npc_groups.name: Binary-7 "Maintenance" Cult
npc_groups.lettering: Vertical columns of binary code and circuit diagrams scratched roughly into surfaces.
npc_groups.language_oddities: The language isn't meant to be read with eyes; it is designed to be felt. The depth of the scratches indicates "volume" or importance.
npc_groups.signage_physical_form: Recycled octagonal hull-plating or scraps of sheet metal. The text is "written" using industrial plasma cutters or heavy-duty welding torches.
npc_groups.communication_quirks: Obsessively practical. They don't believe in adjectives. A sign won't say "Danger: High Voltage," it will simply say "STAY. LETHAL. ENERGY."
npc_groups.common_appearance: Industrial greys and metal plates integrated into bodies; often wear scavenged utility harnesses and tool rigs.
npc_groups.demeanor: Extremely practical and matter‑of‑fact internally; brusque and blunt with outsiders.

npc_groups.name: The Jelly-Kin of Ooze-9
npc_groups.lettering: Swirls of glowing, viscous slime that slowly shifts and pulses.
npc_groups.language_oddities: The language is "living." Because the bacteria in the slime are alive, the signs occasionally "drift," meaning a sign pointing to the Armory might slide six inches down the wall over the course of a week.
npc_groups.signage_physical_form: Translucent glass petri-dishes or sealed plastic pouches filled with neon-green liquid. They are often suction-cupped to doors.
npc_groups.communication_quirks: They are unfailingly cheerful and laid-back, even in dire situations. Their signs often include unsolicited advice or "fun facts" that have nothing to do with the room.
npc_groups.common_appearance: Gelatinous humanoid shapes with luminescent swirls; functional harnesses or containment pods for tools.
npc_groups.demeanor: Cheerful and relaxed toward each other and strangers; often overly friendly.

npc_groups.name: The Fragmented (Exile Spirits)
npc_groups.lettering: Collage-style lettering where every character is stolen from a different source (magazines, old manuals, or other signs).
npc_groups.language_oddities: The signs are often "ghostly"—the Fragmented use a psychic adhesive that makes the signs appear slightly blurry or out of focus unless you look at them through a mirror or a lens.
npc_groups.signage_physical_form: Long scrolls of tattered parchment or synthetic fabric, with letters cut out and glued on. These are often hung crookedly or upside down because "orientation is a physical-plane bias."
npc_groups.communication_quirks: They are conspiratorial and paranoid. They love using riddles and assume everyone is out to steal their "essence." A sign for a bathroom might be a riddle about water and waste.
npc_groups.common_appearance: Semi‑transparent forms with mismatched remnants of cloth and armor; tend to carry patched banners and scrap talismans.
npc_groups.demeanor: Paranoid and suspicious among themselves; distrustful of outsiders, often speaking in riddles.

npc_groups.name: The H-0RS3 "Riders"
npc_groups.lettering: Brightly colored pictograms and stylized emojis that look like ancient Earth street art or 21st-century internet culture.
npc_groups.language_oddities: The language has no grammar. It’s just a sequence of images that the reader is supposed to "vibe" with to understand the meaning.
npc_groups.signage_physical_form: Triangle-shaped stickers or magnets made of neon-colored plastic. They use "Ever-Ink" markers that can only be cleaned with specialized solvents.
